findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() requires a non-null user, disabling conditional passkeys for normal (first-time) login
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Both new call sites use it with `context.getUser()`: in `authenticate()` (line 115) and in `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137). On a regular login the authentication context has no user yet, so the condition is false and `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never invoked. Consequences: the `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI` attribute, the WebAuthn challenge (`AUTH_CHALLENGE_NOTE`), RP id and timeout are never put on the login form, so passkey/conditional-UI login from the initial login page stops working entirely (previously it was enabled exactly in the `context.getUser() == null` case). This also contradicts the existing assertions in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` and `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`, which expect the `webauth` form and `username webauthn` autocomplete on the first login page. The user check should be dropped (the method should only test that the webauthn authenticator exists and passkeys are enabled).

findings.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not match the declared signature
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate()` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` without arguments, but the only declaration in the hierarchy is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (added in this PR, UsernamePasswordForm.java:160); neither `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` nor `AbstractFormAuthenticator` declares a no-arg variant. As written this does not compile. Either add a no-arg overload that only checks `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` (which appears to be the intent here, since the user is already known to be non-null in this branch) or pass `context.getUser()`.

findings.title: Re-authentication now always renders the username form when realm passkeys are enabled, even for users with no passkey
findings.body: The new condition only checks the realm-level passkeys flag, not whether the already-known user actually has a passkey credential. With passkeys enabled on the realm, any re-authentication (e.g. `prompt=login`) will no longer short-circuit the username step; instead the username form is rendered with `usernameHidden=true`, i.e. a page with no input field and just a submit button, for every user including those who have only a password. That is a pointless extra click/step and a confusing screen for all password-only users. Consider also checking that the user has a passwordless WebAuthn credential (as `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm` used to do by returning null when the user has no registered authenticators) before keeping the form.

findings.title: New shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() hook decouples the branch from the null-user guard
findings.body: The branch that builds `new WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean(session, realm, user, ...)` is now guarded by the overridable `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` instead of `user != null`, while `user` is still read from `context.getUser()` above. Any subclass that overrides the hook to return `true` for an unidentified user will pass a `null` user into `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean`, causing an NPE while rendering the login form. Since this is a new protected extension point, the null check on `user` should be kept inside the branch (or documented as a precondition of the hook).

findings.title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey does not cover a password-only user in a passkeys-enabled realm
findings.body: The test name suggests coverage for re-authenticating a user that has no passkey, but it disables passkeys for the whole realm (`setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(FALSE)`), so it only verifies that WebAuthn markup is absent when the realm feature is off. The behaviour actually changed by this PR - passkey/conditional-UI markup is now rendered during re-authentication whenever the realm has passkeys enabled, regardless of whether the known user owns a passkey credential (see `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` returning `false`, which removes the previous "no registered authenticators" short-circuit) - remains untested. Add a case with passkeys enabled on the realm and a user holding only a password.

findings.title: try/catch(Exception) around findElement can silently pass on unrelated WebDriver errors
findings.body: The 'webauthn elements not available' checks are implemented as `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) { }`. Any exception other than `NoSuchElementException` (e.g. `StaleElementReferenceException`, `TimeoutException`, a session error) is swallowed and the assertion silently passes, so the test can report success without having verified anything. Use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(...))` as done elsewhere in these tests.
